extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators, higher-education and K-12 administrators, compliance officers, legal counsel for educational institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria governing when a Title IX Coordinator should initiate a complaint (grievance procedure) in the absence of a complainant, following withdrawal of allegations, or after termination/absence of an informal resolution. Focuses on the factors to consider, the decision standard, and procedural requirements when initiating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (1): Complainant's request not to proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant's request not to proceed with initiation of a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not enumerated in the July 2022 NPRM preamble as a separate factor, the Department requires Title IX Coordinators to consider a complainant's expressed request not to proceed when weighing whether to initiate a complaint, consistent with the recipient's obligation to ensure an education program free from sex discrimination (final §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (2): Complainant's reasonable safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant's reasonable safety concerns regarding initiation of a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Title IX Coordinator must take a complainant's reasonable safety concerns into account and these concerns are 'paramount' in weighing whether to initiate a complaint. If the Coordinator decides to initiate, paragraph (f)(1)(vi) requires notification to the complainant prior to initiation and appropriate steps to address reasonable safety concerns (examples: offering escorts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (3): Risk of additional acts if not initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk that additional acts of sex discrimination would occur if a complaint is not initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether there have been other reports/complaints against the respondent or a pattern that suggests risk of future discrimination; such circumstances weigh in favor of initiating a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (4): Severity of the alleged sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The severity of the alleged sex discrimination, including whether the discrimination, if established, would require removal of a respondent from campus or imposition of another disciplinary sanction to end the discrimination and prevent its recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encompasses seriousness such as violent acts, threats, use of a weapon, or conduct likely to require significant disciplinary action; greater severity supports initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (5): Age and relationship of the parties (including employee status)
rubrics_metrics.description: The age and relationship of the parties, including whether the respondent is an employee of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator should consider power imbalances (for example, employee-student relationships) which might increase the likelihood that initiating a complaint is necessary to address the workplace or learning environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (6): Scope of the alleged sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the alleged sex discrimination, including information suggesting a pattern, ongoing sex discrimination, or sex discrimination alleged to have impacted multiple individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations affecting multiple individuals or indicating widespread/ongoing conduct (e.g., hostile environment) weigh toward initiation to protect equal access of the broader educational community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (7): Availability of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker in determining whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether evidence exists or is likely to be available (including evidence only the complainant can supply). Lack or unavailability of evidence can weigh against initiating a complaint; however, the Title IX Coordinator is not making a determination of whether discrimination occurred at this stage and remains required to take other appropriate prompt/effective steps to prevent recurrence (see §106.44(f)(1)(vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor (8): Whether the recipient could end discrimination without grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the recipient could end the alleged sex discrimination and prevent its recurrence without initiating its grievance procedures under §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other mechanisms (e.g., collective bargaining remedies, policy/practice changes) can adequately end and prevent recurrence, that may counsel against initiating a formal Title IX grievance. This factor is particularly relevant when there is no identifiable respondent (e.g., policy/practice-based discrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision standard to initiate a complaint (imminent/serious threat or prevents equal access)
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering at minimum the eight enumerated factors and any other relevant information, a Title IX Coordinator must determine whether the conduct as alleged (1) presents an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of the complainant or other person; or (2) prevents the recipient from ensuring equal access on the basis of sex to its education program or activity (final §106.44(f)(1)(v)(B)). If neither condition is met, the Coordinator must not initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow, fact-specific threshold: recipients should only initiate grievance procedures without the complainant in very limited circumstances. Events postdating the alleged conduct (e.g., respondent resigns/transfers) that ameliorate risk may mean initiation is not necessary. The same risk assessment standard used for emergency removal applies for assessing imminent/serious threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and addressing safety concerns prior to initiation (paragraph (f)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Title IX Coordinator initiates a complaint under paragraph (f)(1)(v), the Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant before doing so and appropriately address reasonable concerns related to the complainant's safety or the safety of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement ensures complainants are aware a complaint is being initiated and gives them opportunity to raise safety concerns (example: offering an escort). This aims to reduce harms when initiating over a complainant's objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial assessment is a threshold determination, not a credibility determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's initial assessment under §106.44(f)(1)(v) is a threshold determination required to satisfy the recipient's obligation under Title IX to ensure equal educational access, but it is not a credibility determination or an assessment of whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator should consider reported information 'as alleged' and may rely on information received with the report or from conversations with the complainant; this initial assessment generally will not require a formal investigation. The Coordinator may consider other information reasonably known from experience overseeing compliance or similar prior complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to take prompt and effective steps when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must take 'other appropriate prompt and effective steps' to end sex discrimination, in addition to the listed actions, when notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, but only when the Title IX Coordinator reasonably determines the conduct could constitute sex discrimination under paragraph (f)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified that these steps are not required for reports that do not plausibly allege sex discrimination; recipients have flexibility in how to respond outside grievance procedures. Coordinators should use their specialized knowledge to assess alleged conduct and determine appropriate non-grievance actions to end or prevent recurrence without punishing respondents outside established procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible consideration and other relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: The eight enumerated factors are minimum required considerations; a Title IX Coordinator may consider other information known to them that could be relevant to the decision whether to initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits evaluative discretion—Coordinators may weigh case-specific details beyond the enumerated factors, consistent with the duty to ensure equal access and to respect complainant safety and autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to parents/legal representatives and protection of parental and respondent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When a parent, guardian, or authorized legal representative has legal rights to act on behalf of a complainant or other person, the Title IX Coordinator should permit such participation and generally defer to the parent except in cases of serious threat to the child's health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination with parents is permitted; deference to parents is appropriate where they have legal authority, except when immediate protective action is necessary (e.g., potential physical harm or suicidality). Coordinators must also consider respondents' procedural and constitutional protections (including First Amendment considerations) when deciding to initiate.
